title: Read Your First Sentence
intro: Everything so far — the letters, the diacritics, the article, the conventions — comes together in one line. This is the opening of Saadia's Tafsir, Genesis 1:1, in his own Judeo-Arabic. We'll take it one word at a time, letter by letter, until the whole sentence is yours. Then you step into the reader.

sentence.ja: אול מא כ׳לק אללה אלסמאואת ואלארץ׳
sentence.translit: awwal mā khalaq Allāh as-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ
sentence.en: The first thing God created: the heavens and the earth.

words.note: Three letters you know from Lesson 1. The ו does double duty as the doubled w.
אול מא together = "the first thing that…" — Saadia's Arabic way into בראשית.
The gershayim on כ makes kh (خ) — Lesson 2. Root √ḫ-l-q; this is Saadia's word for Hebrew ברא. Drop the dot and you'd see plain כלק (Lesson 4).
It opens with אל, but here that isn't the article — it's the name Allāh itself.
אל = the (Lesson 3); ס is a sun letter, so it's said as-samāwāt. The ־את ending is the plural: heavens.
ו = and, אל = the, ארץ׳ = arḍ. The dot on the final ץ makes ض (emphatic d) — Lesson 2.
